# Project Kickoff Checklist

## Purpose
This checklist ensures that all essential activities are completed during project kickoff to set the project up for success. Use this checklist at the beginning of the planning phase after the project has been approved to move forward from initiation.

## Pre-Kickoff Preparation
- [ ] Project One-pager completed and approved
- [ ] Stakeholders identified and invited to kickoff meeting
- [ ] Team members identified and confirmed availability
- [ ] Kickoff meeting scheduled with adequate time (suggest 90-120 minutes)
- [ ] Kickoff agenda distributed to all participants

## Kickoff Meeting Activities
- [ ] Project Manager facilitates introductions and role clarifications
- [ ] Product Manager presents project vision, goals, and success metrics
- [ ] Business Analyst (if applicable) reviews detailed requirements
- [ ] UX Designer (if applicable) presents design approach and user research insights
- [ ] Developers discuss technical approach and architecture considerations
- [ ] QA Lead outlines testing strategy and quality standards
- [ ] DevOps Engineer reviews infrastructure and deployment approach
- [ ] Release Manager presents release timeline and milestones
- [ ] Team discusses and confirms Definition of Done (DoD)
- [ ] Initial risks and dependencies identified and documented
- [ ] Communication plan and meeting cadence agreed upon

## Post-Kickoff Actions
- [ ] Meeting notes and action items documented and shared
- [ ] Project repository or workspace created
- [ ] Project board set up with initial backlog items
- [ ] Communication channels established (e.g., Slack, Teams)
- [ ] Risk register initialized with identified risks
- [ ] First sprint planning meeting scheduled
- [ ] Stakeholder communication plan finalized and shared
- [ ] All team members have access to necessary tools and resources

## Stakeholder Alignment
- [ ] All stakeholders understand project scope and timeline
- [ ] Roles and responsibilities are clear to all participants
- [ ] Decision-making authority and escalation paths defined
- [ ] Review and approval gates confirmed with stakeholders

## Documentation
- [ ] Project charter or one-pager added to project repository
- [ ] Kickoff meeting notes stored in accessible location
- [ ] Action items assigned with owners and due dates
- [ ] Initial project plan or roadmap published and shared

## Success Criteria
The kickoff is complete when:
- All team members understand their roles and the project goals
- Initial backlog and sprint plan are established
- Communication cadence is agreed upon and scheduled
- All necessary resources and access are in place
- Stakeholders are aligned on scope, timeline, and success metrics
